paragraphs.sourceText: Physical activity does the body good, and there's growing evidence that it helps the brain too. Researchers in the Netherlands report that children who get more exercise, whether at school or on their own, 26 to have higher GPAs and better scores on standardized tests. In a 27 of 14 studies that looked at physical activity and academic 28 , investigators found that the more children moved, the better their grades were in school, 29 in the basic subjects of math, English and reading.
paragraphs.translationZh: 体力活动对身体有好处，而且越来越多的证据表明它也对大脑有帮助。荷兰的研究人员报告说，无论是在学校还是自己进行更多锻炼的孩子，平均绩点（GPA）和标准化考试成绩往往更高。在对 14 项关注身体活动和学习成绩的研究进行审查后，调查人员发现，孩子运动得越多，他们在学校的成绩就越好，特别是在数学、英语和阅读等基础科目上。

paragraphs.sourceText: The data will certainly fuel the ongoing debate over whether physical education classes should be cut as schools struggle to 30 on smaller budgets. The arguments against physical education have included concerns that gym time may be taking away from study time. With standardized test scores in the U.S. 31 in recent years, some administrators believe students need to spend more time in the classroom instead of on the playground. But as these findings show, exercise and academics may not be 32 exclusive. Physical activity can improve blood 33 to the brain, fueling memory, attention and creativity, which are 34 to learning. And exercise releases hormones that can improve 35 and relieve stress, which can also help learning. So while it may seem as if kids are just exercising their bodies when they're running around, they may actually be exercising their brains as well.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些数据肯定会加剧正在进行的关于是否应该削减体育课程的争论，因为学校难以在较小的预算下生存。反对体育教育的论点包括担心健身时间可能会占用学习时间。近年来，随着美国标准化考试成绩的下降，一些管理人员认为学生需要花更多时间在课堂上，而不是在操场上。但正如这些研究结果表明的那样，锻炼和学术可能并不相互排斥。体力活动可以改善大脑的血液流动，增强记忆力、注意力和创造力，这对学习至关重要。而且运动会释放可以改善情绪、缓解压力的激素，这也有助于学习。因此，虽然孩子们在奔跑时似乎只是在锻炼身体，但实际上他们也可能在锻炼大脑。

paragraphs.sourceText: Finding the Right Home—and Contentment, Too
paragraphs.translationZh: 找到合适的家——也能感到满足

paragraphs.sourceText: A. When your elderly relative needs to enter some sort of long-term care facility—a moment few parents or children approach without fear—what you would like is to have everything made clear.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：当您年长的亲戚需要进入某种长期护理机构时（很少有父母或孩子会无所畏惧地接近），您希望一切都清楚。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. Does assisted living really mark a great improvement over a nursing home, or has the industry simply hired better interior designers? Are nursing homes as bad as people fear, or is that an out-moded stereotype（固定看法)? Can doing one's homework really steer families to the best places? It is genuinely hard to know.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 辅助生活真的标志着疗养院的巨大进步，还是该行业只是聘请了更好的室内设计师？疗养院真的像人们担心的那么糟糕吗，还是这是一种过时的刻板印象？做功课真的能引导家庭走向最好的地方吗？这确实很难知道。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. I am about to make things more complicated by suggesting that what kind of facility an older person lives in may matter less than we have assumed. And that the characteristics adult children look for when they begin the search are not necessarily the things that make a difference to the people who are going to move in. I am not talking about the quality of care, let me hastily add. Nobody flourishes in a gloomy environment with irresponsible staff and a poor safety record. But an accumulating body of research indicates that some distinctions between one type of elder care and another have little real bearing on how well residents do.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 我想让事情变得更加复杂，因为我认为老年人住在什么样的设施中可能没有我们想象的那么重要。成年子女在开始寻找时所寻找的特征不一定会对即将搬进来的人产生影响。我不是在谈论护理质量，让我匆忙补充一下。在员工不负责任、安全记录不佳的阴暗环境中，没有人能够蓬勃发展。但越来越多的研究表明，一种老年护理方式与另一种老年护理方式之间的一些区别对于居民的生活质量几乎没有真正的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. The most recent of these studies, published in The journal of Applied Gerontology, surveyed 150 Connecticut residents of assisted living, nursing homes and smaller residential care homes （known in some states as board and care homes or adult care homes). Researchers from the University of Connecticut Health Center asked the residents a large number of questions about their quality of life, emotional well-being and social interaction, as well as about the quality of the facilities.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 最近发表在《应用老年学杂志》上的研究调查了 150 名康涅狄格州辅助生活院、疗养院和小型住宅护理院（在某些州称为寄宿护理院或成人护理院）的居民。康涅狄格大学健康中心的研究人员向居民询问了大量有关他们的生活质量、情绪健康和社交互动以及设施质量的问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. “We thought we would see differences based on the housing types,” said the lead author of the study,Julie Robison, an associate professor of medicine at the university. A reasonable assumption—don't families struggle to avoid nursing homes and suffer real guilt if they can't?
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 该研究的主要作者、该大学医学副教授朱莉·罗宾逊 (Julie Robison) 表示：“我们认为，我们会根据住房类型看到差异。”一个合理的假设是，家庭是否会努力避开疗养院，如果不能的话，他们不会感到真正的内疚吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: F. In the initial results, assisted living residents did paint the most positive picture. They were less likely to report symptoms of depression than those in the other facilities, for instance, and less likely to be bored or lonely. They scored higher on social interaction.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 在初步结果中，辅助生活居民确实描绘了最积极的景象。例如，与其他设施中的人相比，他们报告抑郁症状的可能性较小，也不太可能感到无聊或孤独。他们在社交互动方面得分更高。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. But when the researchers plugged in a number of other variables, such differences disappeared. It is not the housing type, they found, that creates differences in residents' responses. “It is the characteristics of the specific environment they are in, combined with their own personal characteristics—how healthy they feel they are, their age and marital status,” Dr. Robison explained. Whether residents felt involved in the decision to move and how long they had lived there also proved significant.
paragraphs.translationZh: G.但是当研究人员插入一些其他变量时，这种差异就消失了。他们发现，造成居民反应差异的并不是住房类型。 “这是他们所处的特定环境的特征，结合他们自己的个人特征——他们感觉自己的健康程度、年龄和婚姻状况，”罗宾逊博士解释说。事实证明，居民是否愿意参与搬迁决定以及他们在那里住了多久也很重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. An elderly person who describes herself as in poor health, therefore, might be no less depressed in assisted living （even if her children preferred it) than in a nursing home. A person who had input into where he would move and has had time to adapt to it might do as well in a nursing home as in a small residential care home, other factors being equal. It is an interaction between the person and the place, not the sort of place in itself, that leads to better or worse experiences.“You can't just say,'Let's put this person in a residential care home instead of a nursing home—she will be much better off,'” Dr. Robison said. What matters, she added, “is a combination of what people bring in with them, and what they find there.”
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 因此，一位自称健康状况不佳的老人在辅助生活中（即使她的孩子们更愿意）可能会比在疗养院中感到沮丧。如果一个人已经决定要搬到哪里，并且有时间去适应，那么在其他因素相同的情况下，他在疗养院的表现可能和在小型养老院的表现一样好。导致更好或更差体验的是人与地方之间的互动，而不是地方本身。“你不能只是说，‘让我们把这个人安置在住宅护理院而不是疗养院——她会过得更好，’”罗宾逊博士说。她补充道，重要的是“人们带来的东西和他们在那里发现的东西的结合。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Such findings, which run counter to common sense, have surfaced before. In a multi-state study of assisted living, for instance, University of North Carolina researchers found that a host of variables—the facility's type, size or age； whether a chain owned it；how attractive the neighborhood was—had no significant relationship to how the residents fared in terms of illness, mental decline, hospitalizations or mortality. What mattered most was the residents' physical health and mental status. What people were like when they came in had greater consequence than what happened once they were there.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一、此类违背常理的调查结果以前曾出现过。例如，在一项关于辅助生活的多州研究中，北卡罗来纳大学的研究人员发现，许多变量——设施的类型、规模或年龄；是否为连锁店所有；社区的吸引力如何——与居民在疾病、智力衰退、住院或死亡率方面的表现没有显着关系。最重要的是居民的身体健康和精神状态。人们进来时的样子比他们到达那里后所发生的事情具有更大的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. As I was considering all this, a press release from a respected research firm crossed my desk, announcing that the five-star rating system that Medicare developed in 2008 to help families compare nursing home quality also has little relationship to how satisfied its residents or their family members are. As a matter of fact, consumers expressed higher satisfaction with the one-star facilities, the lowest rated, than with the five-star ones. （More on this study and the star ratings will appear in a subsequent post.)
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 当我考虑这一切时，我的办公桌上摆着一家受人尊敬的研究公司的新闻稿，宣布 Medicare 于 2008 年开发的五星级评级系统，旨在帮助家庭比较疗养院的质量，但与居民或其家庭成员的满意度几乎没有关系。事实上，消费者对评分最低的一星级设施的满意度高于五星级设施。 （更多关于这项研究和星级评定的信息将出现在后续的帖子中。）

paragraphs.sourceText: K. Before we collectively tear our hair out—how are we supposed to find our way in a landscape this confusing?—here is a thought from Dr. Philip Sloane, a geriatrician（老年病学专家)at the University of North Carolina :“In a way, that could be liberating for families.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 在我们集体奋力拼搏之前——我们该如何在如此混乱的环境中找到出路？——这是北卡罗来纳大学老年病学专家菲利普·斯隆博士的一个想法：“在某种程度上，这可能会为家庭带来解放。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L. Of course, sons and daughters want to visit the facilities, talk to the administrators and residents and other families, and do everything possible to fulfill their duties. But perhaps they don't have to turn themselves into private investigators or Congressional subcommittees. “Families can look a bit more for where the residents are going to be happy,” Dr. Sloane said. And involving the future resident in the process can be very important.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 当然，儿女们想要参观这些设施，与管理人员、居民和其他家庭交谈，并尽一切可能履行自己的职责。但也许他们不必把自己变成私人调查员或国会小组委员会。 “家庭可以更多地关注居民会感到幸福的地方，”斯隆博士说。让未来的居民参与这个过程可能非常重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. We all have our own ideas about what would bring our parents happiness. They have their ideas, too. A friend recently took her mother to visit an expensive assisted living/nursing home near my town. I have seen this place—it is elegant, inside and out. But nobody greeted the daughter and mother when they arrived, though the visit had been planned；nobody introduced them to the other residents. When they had lunch in the dining room, they sat alone at a table.
paragraphs.translationZh: M. 对于什么能给父母带来幸福，我们都有自己的想法。他们也有自己的想法。一位朋友最近带她的母亲参观了我镇附近一家昂贵的辅助生活/疗养院。我见过这个地方——里里外外都很优雅。但当女儿和母亲到达时，没有人向他们打招呼，尽管这次访问是有计划的；也没有人把他们介绍给其他居民。当他们在餐厅吃午饭时，他们独自坐在一张桌子旁。

paragraphs.sourceText: N. The daughter feared her mother would be ignored there, and so she decided to move her into a more welcoming facility. Based on what is emerging from some of this research, that might have been as rational a way as any to reach a decision.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 女儿担心她的母亲在那里会被忽视，因此她决定将她搬到一个更受欢迎的设施中。根据这项研究的一些结果，这可能是做出决定的一种理性方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Many people feel guilty when they cannot find a place other than a nursing home for their parents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 当许多人无法为父母找到疗养院以外的地方时，他们会感到内疚。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37.Though it helps for children to investigate care facilities, involving their parents in the decision-making process may prove very important.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37.虽然这有助于儿童调查护理机构，但让父母参与决策过程可能非常重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38.It is really difficult to tell if assisted living is better than a nursing home.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38.很难说辅助生活是否比疗养院更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39.How a resident feels depends on an interaction between themselves and the care facility they live in.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 居民的感受取决于他们与所居住的护理机构之间的互动。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40.The author thinks her friend made a rational decision in choosing a more hospitable place over an apparently elegant assisted living home.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40.提交人认为她的朋友做出了理性的决定，选择了一个更热情好客的地方，而不是一个看似优雅的辅助生活之家。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41.The system Medicare developed to rate nursing home quality is of little help to finding a satisfactory place.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41.医疗保险开发的用于评估疗养院质量的系统对找到满意的地方几乎没有帮助。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42.At first the researchers of the most recent study found residents in assisted living facilities gave higher scores on social interaction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 最近研究的研究人员首先发现辅助生活设施中的居民在社交互动方面得分较高。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43.What kind of care facility old people live in may be less important than we think.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43.老年人住在什么样的护理机构，可能没有我们想象的那么重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44.The findings of the latest research were similar to an earlier multi-state study of assisted living.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 最新研究的结果与早期的一项多州辅助生活研究相似。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45.A resident's satisfaction with a care facility has much to do with whether they had participated in the decision to move in and how long they had stayed there.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45.居民对护理机构的满意度很大程度上取决于他们是否参与了搬入的决定以及在那里停留了多长时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly sophisticated, there are growing concerns that robots could become a threat. This danger can be avoided, according to computer science professor Stuart Russell, if we figure out how to turn human values into a programmable code.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着人工智能 (AI) 变得越来越复杂，人们越来越担心机器人可能成为威胁。计算机科学教授斯图尔特·拉塞尔认为，如果我们弄清楚如何将人类价值观转化为可编程代码，这种危险就可以避免。

paragraphs.sourceText: Russell argues that as robots take on more complicated tasks, it's necessary to translate our morals into AI language.
paragraphs.translationZh: 拉塞尔认为，随着机器人承担更复杂的任务，有必要将我们的道德转化为人工智能语言。

paragraphs.sourceText: For example, if a robot does chores around the house, you wouldn't want it to put the pet cat in the oven to make dinner for the hungry children. “You would want that robot preloaded with a good set of values,” said Russell.
paragraphs.translationZh: 例如，如果机器人在房子周围做家务，你不会希望它把宠物猫放在烤箱里为饥饿的孩子们做晚餐。 “你会希望机器人预先加载一组良好的值，”拉塞尔说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some robots are already programmed with basic human values. For example, mobile robots have been programmed to keep a comfortable distance from humans. Obviously there are cultural differences, but if you were talking to another person and they came up close in your personal space, you wouldn't think that's the kind of thing a properly brought-up person would do.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一些机器人已经被编程了基本的人类价值观。例如，移动机器人已被编程为与人类保持舒适的距离。显然存在文化差异，但如果你正在与另一个人交谈并且他们靠近你的个人空间，你不会认为这是一个有教养的人会做的事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: It will be possible to create more sophisticated moral machines, if only we can find a way to set out human values as clear rules.
paragraphs.translationZh: 只要我们能够找到一种方法将人类价值观制定为明确的规则，就有可能创造出更复杂的道德机器。

paragraphs.sourceText: Robots could also learn values from drawing patterns from large sets of data on human behavior. They are dangerous only if programmers are careless.
paragraphs.translationZh: 机器人还可以通过从大量人类行为数据中绘制模式来学习价值。只有当程序员不小心时它们才是危险的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The biggest concern with robots going against human values is that human beings fail to do sufficient testing and they've produced a system that will break some kind of taboo（禁忌).
paragraphs.translationZh: 对机器人违背人类价值观的最大担忧是，人类未能进行足够的测试，而他们创造了一个会打破某种禁忌的系统。

paragraphs.sourceText: One simple check would be to program a robot to check the correct course of action with a human when presented with an unusual situation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一种简单的检查是对机器人进行编程，以在遇到异常情况时检查人类的正确行动方案。

paragraphs.sourceText: If the robot is unsure whether an animal is suitable for the microwave, it has the opportunity to stop, send out beeps（嘟嘟声), and ask for directions from a human. If we humans aren't quite sure about a decision, we go and ask somebody else.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果机器人不确定动物是否适合使用微波炉，它有机会停下来，发出嘟嘟声，并向人类询问方向。如果我们人类对某个决定不太确定，我们会去询问其他人。

paragraphs.sourceText: The most difficult step in programming values will be deciding exactly what we believe in moral, and how to create a set of ethical rules. But if we come up with an answer, robots could be good for humanity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 制定价值观最困难的一步是准确决定我们相信什么道德，以及如何制定一套道德规则。但如果我们找到答案，机器人可能会给人类带来好处。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why do some people live to be older than others? You know the standard explanations: keeping a moderate diet, engaging in regular exercise, etc. But what effect does your personality have on your longevity（长寿）?Do some kinds of personalities lead to longer lives? A new study in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society looked at this question by examining the personality characteristics of 246 children of people who had lived to be at least 100.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么有些人比其他人活得更老？你知道标准的解释：保持适度饮食、定期锻炼等。但是你的性格对你的长寿有什么影响？某些性格会导致长寿吗？ 《美国老年医学会杂志》上的一项新研究通过检查 246 名活到 100 岁以上的人的孩子的性格特征来解决这个问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The study shows that those living the longest are more outgoing, more active and less neurotic（神经质的) than other people. Long-living women are also more likely to be sympathetic and cooperative than women with a normal life span. These findings are in agreement with what you would expect from the evolutionary theory: those who like to make friends and help others can gather enough resources to make it through tough times.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究表明，寿命最长的人比其他人更外向、更活跃、更少神经质。与正常寿命的女性相比，长寿的女性也更有可能表现出同情心和合作精神。这些发现与你对进化论的期望是一致的：那些喜欢交朋友和帮助别人的人可以收集足够的资源来度过困难时期。

paragraphs.sourceText: Interestingly, however, other characteristics that you might consider advantageous had no impact on whether study participants were likely to live longer. Those who were more self-disciplined, for instance, were no more likely to live to be very old. Also, being open to new ideas had no relationship to long life, which might explain all those bad-tempered old people who are fixed in their ways.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而有趣的是，您可能认为有利的其他特征对研究参与者是否可能活得更长没有影响。例如，那些更加自律的人不太可能活到很老。此外，对新思想持开放态度与长寿无关，这或许可以解释为什么那些脾气暴躁、固守己见的老人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Whether you can successfully change your personality as an adult is the subject of a longstanding psychological debate. But the new paper suggests that if you want long life, you should strive to be as outgoing as possible.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为一个成年人，是否能够成功地改变自己的性格是一个长期的心理争论的主题。但这篇新论文建议，如果你想长寿，你应该努力变得尽可能外向。

paragraphs.sourceText: Unfortunately, another recent study shows that your mother's personality may also help determine your longevity. That study looked at nearly 28,000 Norwegian mothers and found that those moms who were more anxious, depressed and angry were more likely to feed their kids unhealthy diets. Patterns of childhood eating can be hard to break when we're adults, which may mean that kids of depressed moms end up dying younger.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不幸的是，最近的另一项研究表明，你母亲的性格也可能有助于决定你的寿命。这项研究对近 28,000 名挪威母亲进行了调查，发现那些更加焦虑、抑郁和愤怒的母亲更有可能给孩子提供不健康的饮食。当我们成年后，童年的饮食模式可能很难打破，这可能意味着抑郁妈妈的孩子最终会更早去世。

paragraphs.sourceText: Personality isn't destiny（命运), and everyone knows that individuals can learn to change. But both studies show that long life isn't just a matter of your physical health but of your mental health.
paragraphs.translationZh: 个性不是命运，每个人都知道个人可以学会改变。但这两项研究都表明，长寿不仅与身体健康有关，还与心理健康有关。
